title: Redwood POC scoping with Springdale Health - security pilot
next_steps: SE to run 48-hour benchmark on POC data (staging) and share results (due 2027-10-28)
AE to send SOC 2 & ISO artifacts + security deck link by 2027-10-22
Customer to provide sample workload & SLA targets by 2027-10-25
Schedule follow-up to review benchmarks w/ Priya and Tom (tentative 2027-11-02)
action_items: Marcus Li: run end-to-end latency & throughput benchmark on 4-node dedicated pool (due 2027-10-28)
Lena Torres: send SOC2 report and ISO whitepaper + security deck link (due 2027-10-22)
Priya Shah: share list of required audit fields and retention policy (due 2027-10-25)
Elena Martinez: provide network diagram and VPC peering constraints (due 2027-10-25)
summary: POC scoping focused on security/compliance requirements for a small pilot (4-6 week) to validate latency/cost and auditability. Customer requires SOC 2 + ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC for admin/ops, detailed audit logs + retention, and optional KMS/HSM encryption for keys. SE to run benchmarks on a staging workload, AE to share security docs, and customer to provide workloads and timeline. Success criteria agreed: sustained 95th p50 latency under 250ms for single-request conversational flows, end-to-end 99% availability for test window, and complete traceable audit logs + SSO integration validated.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-21
Time: 16:00 UTC / 09:00 PT
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Lena Torres (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (CISO, Springdale), Tom Reynolds (Head of AI), Elena Martinez (IT Ops), Abe Chen (Compliance)
Shared links: security deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/pilot-security), benchmark sheet (redwood://bench/59321)

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a friday, appreciate it. i'm lena, account exec on the springdale deal, and marcus is our se. quick check on audio?
[00:12] Tom: good here, can you hear me fine, yes.
[00:16] Marcus: yep loud and clear.
[00:18] Priya: good, thanks.

[00:25] Lena: quick agenda — we want to align on success criteria for the poc, sizing and benchmark approach, and the security/compliance checklist you need to sign off a pilot. we'll capture next steps and owners.

[01:02] Tom: sounds good. to give context, we're piloting a conversational triage assistant in our call centers — about 10k conversations/day expected in pilot peak, average ctx ~600 tokens per convo, spikey distribution. main thing is security — PHI touches possible — and auditability for compliance.

[01:35] Marcus: ok got it, so 10k conv/day, ~600 tokens average. for benchmarks we'd want to simulate both single interactive flows (low latency) and backfill/batch embedding workloads. is the 600 tokens typical across the flow or includes pre/post context?

[01:48] Tom: includes preamble + user messages; kv cache hit expected maybe 40% once flow warms up.

[02:05] Priya: and from security side we require SOC 2 type 2 evidence, ISO 27001 attestation ideally, sso via saml,rbac for least privilege, and audit logs that show per-request user-id mapping. retention needs are 7 years for certain audit trails but for pilot we could start with 1 year if we prove exportability.

[02:38] Marcus: understood. for POC we typically provide SOC2 report and SSAE artifacts, plus a security deck. we also have options for private deployment (VPC) or dedicated capacity. for sso we support saml 2.0 and oidc, and you can map groups to roles — our console exposes RBAC with admin/operator/dev roles.

[03:05] Priya: do you have attestation documents public or do you share on-demand?
[03:10] Lena: we can share SOC 2 and ISO artifacts under an NDA — i'll send them after this call, link included in next steps.

[03:22] Abe: any third-party pen-test results?
[03:25] Marcus: we have a summary and scope of recent pentests, and we can provide the redacted report. again, we'll route through your security mailbox.

[04:00] Tom: on performance, our target for the pilot is p95 under 400ms for single request generation and p50 around 150-200ms. we also want throughput to handle burst of 100 concurrent flows.

[04:18] Marcus: ok practical question — are you open to dedicated reserved pool (dedicated) for predictable latency vs hosted where we route across shared capacity?

[04:28] Tom: prefer dedicated for the pilot if cost is reasonable. procurement wants predictability.

[04:34] Marcus: perfect — for dedicated we can size a 4-GPU NVidia A100-ish pool (or equivalent) and run continuous batching. for 10k conv/day and 600 tokens average, rough estimate is X tokens/day — we will provide exact numeric in the benchmark sheet.

[04:58] Priya: about keys — we need customer-managed keys (kms/hsm). is that supported on private?

[05:05] Marcus: yes for Private and Dedicated we offer KMS integration; for hosted we support envelope encryption and optional bring-your-own-key via cloud KMS in certain regions. there are some limitations around on-prem hsm which we can detail.

[05:27] Lena: quick realism check — for this pilot timeline what were you thinking, tom?

[05:32] Tom: want pilot to start roughly 2 weeks from now and run 4 weeks, so total 6 weeks to decision. security sign-off is gating, so if we can validate SSO and audit logs in week one that would be ideal.

[05:45] Priya: yes week one needs SSO + RBAC + audit log sample export. also need assurance on retention and deletion processes.

[06:10] Marcus: for SSO we can set up a saml test connector — usually takes a day to configure, then demo. audit logs: we emit per-request logs with user mapping, model version, token counts, timestamps — retention configurable. i'll attach a sample log schema to the benchmark sheet.

[06:40] [small crosstalk]

[07:00] Tom: any gotchas with PII/PHI?

[07:05] Marcus: we recommend redaction at ingest or using prefix tokenization; also we support opt-out of data retention in hosted paths and strict isolation in Dedicated. for maximum compliance, Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) is ideal.

[07:30] Priya: what about audit trail exportability — if regulators ask for raw logs can we export in readable format?

[07:36] Marcus: yes exports are available as JSONL with deltas and indexes. retention policies can be set and archived to your S3 bucket. will share the export example.

[08:05] Lena: let's try to align success criteria now — what would you need to mark pilot success?

[08:12] Tom:
- functional: template accuracy for triage (we'll run evals but that's separate)
- performance: p95 latency < 400ms, p50 < 200ms, sustain bursts up to 100 conc flows
- security: SSO integrated, RBAC validated, audit log completeness and retention tested
- cost: projected unit cost within procurement thresholds (we'll verify post-bench)

[08:46] Priya: i also want evidence of background checks and SOC 2.

[08:52] Lena: noted. we'll deliver those.

[09:00] Marcus: on benchmarks — we'll run two primary tests: single-request latency test (50k requests distributed) and throughput test (concurrent sessions up to 150 for headroom). we'll instrument token-level timing and end-to-end from request to response. the benchmark will run in staging mirrored to your expected ctx lengths.

[09:25] Tom: can you include KV cache behaviors? hit rates will matter.

[09:28] Marcus: yes we'll simulate warm-cached and cold-cached runs to show delta. also include quantization variant if you want to reduce cost.

[09:40] Priya: about RBAC — we need separation of duties: ops can't export raw logs without audit approval. can your console do approvals?

[09:50] Marcus: we have role-level entitlements; approval flows can be integrated via workflows, otherwise we can restrict export and require an admin action logged as well. the audit log captures the admin user and IP on export.

[10:12] Lena: procurement question: how long to stand up dedicated capacity?

[10:16] Marcus: provisioning a 4-GPU pool typically takes 2-3 business days once contract and payment are in place; private (VPC) setup longer due to network peering — usually 7-14 days depending on networking approvals.

[10:32] Elena: network — we have strict firewall and only a few egress endpoints allowed, plus strict CIDR ranges. will redwood require inbound peering?

[10:40] Marcus: for VPC peering we need a peering connection and a small set of endpoints; we'll provide exact egress IPs and ports. we can also use private link in supported clouds.

[11:00] Tom: timeline check — if we start week of 10/25, we want SSO test and sample logs by 10/29, benchmarks run 10/30-11/02, and decision meeting around 11/05. is that reasonable?

[11:15] Lena: that's plausible. we'll aim to have docs out tomorrow and se to start bench asap.

[11:22] Priya: one more — do you support long-term retention to on-prem archives in case of legal hold?

[11:27] Marcus: yes we support exports to your S3 or secure FTP; legal hold workflows can be discussed with our compliance team.

[11:40] Abe: will need to see a redacted pentest and SOC 2 report before we let infra team open firewall rules.

[11:47] Lena: yep will send after call via secure link.

[11:52] Tom: anything else on cost controls — any token-level cost breakdowns we can see?

[11:57] Marcus: yes our console provides token-level cost & latency breakdown per route. we can produce a projected TCO for the pilot based on benchmark results.

[12:10] Lena: OK let's recap next steps and owners — marcus to run benchmark and attach sheet, lena to send SOC2/ISO and pentest summary, springdale to provide workload and network diagram. tentative follow-up 11/05 to review results.

[12:30] Tom: that covers it, appreciate the clarity.

[12:34] Priya: thanks all.

[12:36] Lena: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email. bye.

[End of transcript]
